These findings provide a new perspective for in-depth analysis of heterogeneous cell clusters, functions, and regulatory pathways in female floral organs, as well as potential targets for improving maize ear traits.

papers.title: Deep single-cell proteomics reveals cellular heterogeneity in the cold response of Arabidopsis leaves.
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomic analysis at single-cell resolution in complex plant tissues is challenging. Here, we present a highly sensitive single-cell proteomics (SCP) workflow that integrates key steps including single-cell sorting, sample pretreatment, MS detection, and data processing, with specific optimizations tailored for plant cells. Using this customized workflow, we achieved great identification depth, quantifying approximately 4,200 protein groups from a single mesophyll cell. In the proof-of-principle application in the cold response research of Arabidopsis leaves, we achieved accurate cell typing/clustering based on proteomic information at the single-cell level in plants. Moreover, we revealed cell-type-specific differences in cold response and quantified the dynamic changes of cold-responsive proteins at single-cell resolution. Among 100 randomly sorted epidermal cells, two major cell types (guard cell and pavement cell) were identified. The observed discordance at single-cell level between proteome and transcriptome in mesophyll cells further underscores the importance of plant SCP technologies. Our deep plant SCP workflow paves the way for future applications across diverse tissues/organs and enables comprehensive insights into plant biology.

papers.title: Integrated Spatial Multi-Omics Reveals Metabolic Hotspots of Paclitaxel Biosynthesis in Taxus yunnanensis.
papers.abstract: Paclitaxel (Taxol) is a broad-spectrum anticancer drug, but its clinical application is limited by insufficient production and supply. Although previous studies have noted regional differences in paclitaxel metabolism within stem tissues, the spatial compartmentalization characteristics remain unclear due to the lack of effective analytical methods. Here, we first profiled stem segments of a single Taxus yunnanensis stem spanning six longitudinal positions from juvenile (P1) to mature (P6) tissue by DESI-MSI spatial metabolomics. We then integrated spatial metabolomics with Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA-seq at position P2 using three biological replicates, through cross-modality alignment of adjacent sections at the bin level (40 μm). Our findings reveal that intermediate metabolites in the paclitaxel biosynthesis pathway exhibit positive spatial autocorrelation, forming two types of spatial microdomains (metabolic hotspots) with distinct accumulation patterns, one enriched in early scaffold-forming and the other in late side-chain intermediates. Compared with surrounding tissues, these hotspots had relatively higher relative abundancesof paclitaxel intermediates and elevated expression of paclitaxel biosynthesis-related genes, suggesting functional compartmentalization. At hotspot boundaries, ABC transporter genes (such as TyuABCG15) showed higher expression than either inside the hotspots or in the surrounding tissue, suggesting their possible involvement in intercellular transport of paclitaxel intermediates. This study therefore proposes a spatially coordinated multicellular model for paclitaxel biosynthesis, providing new insights into the spatial regulation of plant secondary metabolite biosynthesis and transport.

papers.title: Coordinated cell division and growth drive meristem notch formation in Ceratopteris gametophytes.
papers.abstract: Meristems drive organogenesis and shape plant body plans, yet their morphology and cellular organization vary widely across land plants. Fern gametophytes develop a multicellular meristem that initiates at one flat margin of the prothallus and progressively forms a distinctive concave notch, producing the characteristic cordate gametophyte. Despite its importance for gametophyte growth and sexual organ formation, the cellular basis of meristem notch morphogenesis remains unclear. Here, we address this question in the fern Ceratopteris richardii using long-term time-lapse confocal imaging, chemical perturbations, and quantitative analyses at single-cell resolution. We reconstructed complete cell lineages and generated dynamic maps of cell division, size, growth rate, and collective cell displacement throughout development. Our analyses reveal that position-specific cell proliferation and division patterns, coordinated with differential cell expansion and dynamic cell displacement between the notch-forming lineage and adjacent wing regions, drive notch morphogenesis. Chemical perturbations disrupting microtubule function or cell-cycle progression disrupted notch formation, demonstrating that coordinated cell division and growth are required. Together, these findings establish a quantitative cellular framework for understanding meristem morphogenesis across land plants.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome atlas reveals a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense against Sclerotium rolfsii in Dendrobium officinale.
papers.abstract: Plants employ cell-type-specific transcriptional programs to defend against pathogens, yet the cellular heterogeneity of immune responses in the medicinal orchid Dendrobium officinale Kimura et Migo remains largely unexplored. A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the D. officinale stem base upon Sclerotium rolfsii infection was constructed, profiling over 20 000 cells across 12 and 24 h post-infection. A total of 21 cell clusters were resolved into 6 major cell types-epidermal, ground tissue parenchyma, proliferating, xylem, phloem, and vascular bundle parenchyma cells-with identities validated by fluorescence in situ hybridization. Cell-type-specific analyses revealed that epidermal and phloem cells mounted early defense responses, while xylem cells exhibited the most extensive transcriptional reprogramming at 24 hpi, coinciding with the activation of lignin biosynthesis pathways. WRKY33 was identified as a central transcriptional activator that directly binds W-box motifs in the promoters of lignin biosynthetic genes C4H and HCT, promoting lignin deposition and enhancing disease resistance. Conversely, the nuclear-localized chaperone HSP81 physically interacts with WRKY33 and functions as a broad regulator of multiple transcription factors via co-factor sequestration, thereby compromising defense when overexpressed. These findings uncover a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense in D. officinale, providing a high-resolution cellular framework for understanding plant immunity and offering potential targets for improving disease resistance in this economically valuable species.

papers.title: PlantCCC prioritizes context-specific candidate ligand-receptor communication patterns in plant spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Intercellular communication supports plant development and environmental responses, but its analysis in plant tissues is complicated by cell walls, plasmodesmata, and local tissue architecture. Spatial proximity therefore does not necessarily indicate effective communication. Plant ligand-receptor (L-R) resources also contain expanded gene families, homology-derived mappings, and uneven levels of experimental support. We developed PlantCCC, a spatially aware graph-learning framework that uses a plant L-R database as a candidate search space and combines residual spatial expression enhancement, a directed heterogeneous candidate graph, expression-gated spatial weighting, spatially aware multi-head graph attention, and self-supervised contrastive learning to prioritize context-specific candidate edges. In a semi-synthetic benchmark, PlantCCC distinguished TRUE pairs containing an injected interaction component from CONFOUNDER pairs showing tissue co-localization alone, and remained comparatively robust under dropout perturbation. In poplar stem analyses based on a homology-derived Populus candidate L-R set, and in an independent Arabidopsis Visium HD analysis based on Arabidopsis PlantPhoneDB entries, PlantCCC prioritized candidate L-R axes that were consistent with tissue architecture, spatial expression patterns, and prior evidence for the corresponding signaling modules. PlantCCC provides an interpretable computational framework for prioritizing context-specific candidate cell-cell communication patterns in plant spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptome Analysis Provides New Insights Into B Chromosome Elimination in Sorghum.
papers.abstract: B chromosomes are supernumerary entities found in many plant species, with some exhibiting tissue-specific elimination. In Sorghum purpureosericeum, extensive B chromosome elimination occurs during embryogenesis affecting most of the embryonic organs, leaving the B chromosome maintained mainly in limited regions of meristems. The dynamics of the process and rarity of the transcripts associated with elimination make capturing it challenging. To address this, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on embryos undergoing B chromosome elimination. This approach enabled detection of more B-linked transcripts compared to previous methods. Notably, we identified nuclei with B-specific transcripts, which predominantly clustered in a single cluster in both replicates of B-positive embryos. Further analysis of these clusters revealed three subpopulations with divergent transcriptional profiles. One subpopulation showed gene expression patterns suggesting active elimination of the B chromosome, while the other subpopulations are expected to exhibit regular segregation of the B chromosome and/or preparation for the elimination process. Our analysis provides resolution so far missing in current studies and highlights a clear benefit of the single-cell approaches for studying specific behaviour of the B chromosomes.

papers.title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Identifies Stage-Associated Differences in the Olfactory Epithelium During Natural Sex Reversal in <i>Monopterus albus</i>.
papers.abstract: The rice field eel (Monopterus albus) undergoes natural protogynous sex reversal, but whether peripheral sensory tissues differ across sexual stages remains poorly understood. We used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to characterize the olfactory epithelium (OE) of female, intersex, and male rice field eels. After quality control, 22,959 nuclei were retained and classified into 19 cell populations, including olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs), basal/progenitor, epithelial, mesenchymal, endothelial, and immune populations. OE tissues from five individuals within each sexual stage were pooled prior to nuclei isolation, resulting in one pooled snRNA-Seq library per stage; therefore, between-stage comparisons are interpreted as exploratory and descriptive rather than as independently replicated population-level differences. The relative representation of captured nuclei differed among stages, particularly within the sensory neuronal and basal-cell compartments. Pseudotime analysis placed immature OSNs at relatively early transcriptional states associated with ciliated and microvillous OSN populations, whereas CrOSNs were not continuously connected to the principal iOSN-cOSN/mOSN trajectory. Cell-type-specific analyses identified stage-associated transcriptional differences in basal cells and multiple OSN populations. Predicted cell-cell communication profiles also differed among stages, with male OE showing a larger nominal number of inferred interactions but lower overall predicted interaction strength. Expression patterns of ompa, gng8, and ora4 supported the marker-based annotation of major OSN populations within the dataset. These findings provide an exploratory single-nucleus framework for investigating stage-associated variation in the peripheral olfactory system of M. albus.

papers.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root.
papers.abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory<sup>1</sup>. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals distinct regulatory architectures coordinating carbon assimilation and cyclic electron flow in maize C<sub>4</sub> photosynthesis.
papers.abstract: C<sub>4</sub> photosynthesis arose repeatedly through redeployment of pre-existing regulatory circuitry, yet how a shared regulatory system coordinates its interdependent photosynthetic functions remains unresolved. Here we integrate single-nucleus RNA-seq and sci-ATAC-seq with bulk histone profiles from mesophyll- and bundle sheath-enriched fractions and transcription factor binding profiles obtained in protoplasts. We compare the C<sub>4</sub> shuttle and Calvin-Benson-Bassham cycle with NDH-mediated cyclic electron flow in bundle sheath cells. Selected carbon assimilation loci were associated with differential H3K27me3, whereas the NDH-associated branch showed regulatory inputs linked to DNA binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factors. Dissection of the ZmNdhU promoter identifies a 49 bp DOF-responsive cis element whose activity is sensitive to local sequence context and insertion position in the promoter constructs tested and that supports vascular bundle-associated reporter expression in a heterologous promoter context. Bundle sheath-enriched expression of ZmDOF30 increases NDH-associated expression, cyclic electron flow, leaf ATP content and photosynthetic performance. In a field trial, the transgenic lines showed increased growth and biomass. Comparative analyses revealed lineage-associated variation in predicted promoter-proximal DOF-binding potential within a broader H3K27me3-associated transcription factor background. These findings distinguish regulatory configurations among maize photosynthetic modules and identify DOF-NDH regulation as a candidate route for improving photosynthetic performance in maize, with broader relevance to NADP-ME grasses.

papers.title: ZmAGA1 enhances seed germination through raffinose hydrolysis and ZmSnRK1α-mediated starch mobilization in maize.
papers.abstract:
Background

Raffinose family oligosaccharides are key endogenous factors influencing seed germination, with raffinose as the sole member in maize. However, the mechanisms by which raffinose regulates germination remain largely unexplored.

Results

A metabolite-based genome-wide association study using a maize CUBIC population identifies six candidate genes involved in raffinose metabolism in maize kernel. Among these, ZmAGA1, encoding an alkaline α-galactosidase, is localized in the cytosol and exhibits high expression levels in the embryo during seed germination. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of ZmAGA1 leads to delayed germination, reduced germination rates, and impaired seedling growth. Integrative spatial metabolomics and single-nucleus transcriptomics analyses at 18, 24, 36, and 48 h after imbibition in germinating seeds reveal that ZmAGA1 not only mediates raffinose catabolism and spatiotemporal sugar dynamics, but also positively correlates with ZmαAMY2 and ZmαAMY3 expression in aleurone cells and elevates α-amylase activity. Moreover, ZmAGA1 physically interacts with the energy-sensing kinase ZmSnRK1α in the cytosol, and both genes are co-expressed across embryonic tissues. In zmaga1 protoplasts, ZmSnRK1α shifts toward nuclear enrichment, where it interacts with the transcription factor ZmMYBS1, which directly activates ZmαAMY3 transcription. Consistently, ZmαAMY3 transcript levels are reduced in zmaga1 and zmsnrk1α protoplasts. These findings support a ZmAGA1-ZmSnRK1α-ZmMYBS1 cascade linking raffinose hydrolysis to α-amylase activation during seed germination.

Conclusions

Our integrative spatial-omics analyses reveal that ZmAGA1 facilitates seed germination by modulating sugar metabolism through the hydrolysis of raffinose and via ZmSnRK1α-dependent regulation of starch mobilization, with both processes providing essential energy for seed germination and early seedling establishment in maize.

papers.title: Cis-TERN: a graph-based method to integrate single-cell chromatin accessibility with gene expression data to infer the pseudotime ordering of cells.
papers.abstract:
Motivation

Pseudotime ordering methods computationally arrange individually sequenced cells along a continuous trajectory to infer their progression through biological processes. Chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements is pivotal for orchestrating the timing of gene expression during cellular differentiation. However, data sparsity and discrete grouping imposed by clustering-based approaches, often obscures subtle cell-state transitions and intermediate populations.

Results

Here, we introduce Cis-TERN (Cis-Temporally Encoded Regulation Network), a graph-based method that integrates scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq to infer a pseudotime ordering of cells. Exploiting the fact that distal cis chromatin accessibility often precedes gene activation, Cis-TERN builds a directed bipartite graph between scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cells with edge weights determined by either proximal or distal accessibility. Through network diffusion, Cis-TERN assigns continuous pseudotime scores to all cells. Cis-TERN infers cellular pseudotime without the need for prior biological knowledge, such as specifying a root cell type, thereby enabling unbiased reconstruction of differentiation from data alone. We show that our scores align with known lineages in healthy and tumor-derived hematopoietic cells. Additionally, Cis-TERN is able to trace individual cancer cells back to progenitor cell types. Our approach establishes a framework for leveraging chromatin accessibility and gene expression jointly to learn the timing of cell state progression.

Availability and implementation

Cis-TERN is available at https://github.com/pawelab/Cis-TERN.

papers.title: Single-cell Transcriptome Profiling Reveals Gene Regulatory Networks and Key Genes in the Root Epidermis and Cortical Cells Associated with Early Nodulation in Glycine Max.
papers.abstract: The legume crop soybean forms a symbiosis with rhizobia to fix atmospheric nitrogen (N) in specialized organs called root nodules. However, the mechanisms regulating early infection of the root epidermis and nodule-primordium formation in the cortex for proper nodule formation remain unclear in soybean. Here, we report a single-cell transcriptome analysis of mock- and rhizobia-inoculated soybean roots at 4 days after inoculation, an important control point for autoregulation of nodulation and nodule-primordium formation. We profiled 21,500 cells and detected 12 major cell clusters, and identified 193 infected-cell-specific, 205 epidermis-specific and 180 cortex-specific DEGs. Gene-ontology enrichment and gene-regulatory network analyses uncovered key pathways such as reactive oxygen species-mediated hormone signaling involved in coordinating defense signaling and symbiotic pathways. We also identified and functionally validated an ethylene-activated circuit comprising GmWRKY6.3/6.4 transcription factors and select downstream GmNod19 targets, in which genes act as positive regulators by promoting infection-thread formation during early nodulation, thereby shaping nodule formation. This study showcases how single-cell transcriptomics and gene-regulatory networks provide hypotheses for identification and characterization of previously unappreciated regulatory circuits, broadens our understanding of precise genetic control underlying symbiosis establishment, and underscores how functional diversification of nodulation genes has occurred across legumes.

papers.title: Advances in single-cell proteomics: label-free quantification of over 3500 protein groups from individual Arabidopsis thaliana seedling cells.
Engineering root development with high precision.
papers.abstract: Root development is controlled by dynamic interactions between gene regulation, hormonal signalling, developmental history and environmental inputs, creating multiple layers of control that can be harnessed for engineering. Recent advances in single-cell technologies, spatial transcriptomics and synthetic biology are beginning to resolve root development at the cellular level and enable increasingly precise manipulation of developmental programmes. Here, we discuss how lineage tracing, genetic recording of developmental history, cell-type-specific engineering and programmable genetic circuits can be integrated to understand and control root architecture. We highlight emerging strategies for engineering adaptive and context-dependent developmental behaviours, including history-dependent and reversible response programmes and rewired root-environment interactions. Together, these approaches establish a foundation for programmable and adaptive root system engineering in plants.

papers.title: scPlantAnnotate: an accurate and robust transformer-based model for plant cell type annotation.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Accurate cell type annotation remains a major bottleneck in plant single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), where existing tools are often adapted from animal studies and perform sub-optimally on plant data. The lack of plant-specific computational frameworks limits the construction of plant cell atlases and downstream biological discovery.

Objectives

We develop and evaluate scPlantAnnotate, a Transformer-based reference annotation framework tailored for plant scRNA-seq data, and benchmark it against state-of-the-art deep learning and conventional methods across multiple plant species.

Methods

Species-specific scPlantAnnotate models were trained using curated datasets from Arabidopsis thaliana, Zea mays, Oryza sativa, and Glycine max. We compared scPlantAnnotate with leading baselines under both standard random-split evaluation and a more stringent leave-one-dataset-out setting, which tests robustness to completely unseen datasets and tissue types.

Results

scPlantAnnotate consistently outperforms existing approaches across all four species under random-split evaluation. In the leave-one-dataset-out setting for A. thaliana, where performance drops markedly for all methods due to strong batch effects and dataset heterogeneity, scPlantAnnotate nonetheless achieves the highest Accuracy, Macro-F1, Balanced Accuracy, and Macro-AUROC on average and ranks first on most held-out datasets. These results demonstrate improved robustness to dataset shifts, a critical yet underexplored challenge in plant scRNA-seq analysis. A freely accessible web server enables users to annotate their own datasets using pretrained models.

Conclusion

scPlantAnnotate provides a plant-specific, Transformer-based framework for single-cell annotation that delivers state-of-the-art performance and enhanced robustness to unseen datasets. By addressing limitations of existing tools and enabling scalable reference-based annotation, scPlantAnnotate supports the development of comprehensive plant cell atlases and facilitates broader use of single-cell genomics in plant biology.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptional decoding of iron deficiency responses in maize root tips.
papers.abstract:
Key message

Maize roots respond to iron stress through cell type specificity and enhanced radial transport of Fe-DMA in root cells. Iron (Fe) deficiency, resulting from low Fe solubility in aerated soils, represents a major constraint for crop productivity. Maize (Zea mays), a Strategy II plant, acquires Fe through phytosiderophore (PS)-mediated chelation of rhizospheric Fe (III) and subsequent uptake of Fe (III)-PS complexes. However, cell-type-specific responses governing this process under Fe deficiency remain uncharacterized. Leveraging single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we constructed a root tip atlas using 15,306 high-quality cells from V3 stage primary roots under Fe-sufficient and Fe-deficient conditions, resolving seven distinct cell types. Under iron deficiency stress, significant changes were observed in the cell populations of cortex, epidermis, stele, and xylem. The cortex undergoes functional reprogramming following iron deficiency, with heme-binding and glutathione metabolism-related genes playing crucial roles in the iron deficiency response. Expression analysis of iron homeostasis genes revealed that iron-deficient root tips are associated with the biosynthesis of nicotianamine (NA) and 2'-deoxymugineic acid (DMA) and facilitated radial Fe-chelator transport. Notably, both scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data revealed the downregulation of a FER-like iron deficiency-induced transcription factor (FIT) gene homologous to Arabidopsis AtFIT. This contrasts with the well-established role of AtFIT in Arabidopsis, where it acts as a positive regulator under iron-deficient conditions. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that AtFIT, OsFIT, and ZmFIT may share conserved functions, while their divergent expression patterns could be associated with differences between monocots and dicots. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified cell-type-specific co-expression modules for the cortex, stele, epidermis, and xylem. The stele-specific module was significantly enriched with transcription factors, suggesting its role as a transcriptional regulatory hub for the iron deficiency response. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis revealed that core regulatory transcription factors (ZmWRKY76, ZmbHLH49, ZmMKK9) were distributed across various cell types including epidermis, xylem, phloem, and lateral root cap, indicating that the iron deficiency response is coordinated by a distributed regulatory network where the stele integrates signals and different cell types execute specific functions. In this study, we constructed a transcription map of iron-deficient maize root tips at single-cell resolution, uncovering fundamental adaptation strategies and potential targets for enhancing crop Fe efficiency.

papers.title: ABA and Stomatal Biology: From Transcriptional and Biosynthesis to Multicellular Coordination Across Cell Types.
papers.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) was first identified in plants over six decades ago and is now recognized as one of the central phytohormones in plants, regulating growth, development, and physiological adaptation to environmental changes. In this Centennial Update, we use two influential ABA-related articles published in Plant Physiology in the early 2000s and discuss complementary advances in stress-responsive transcription and ABA biosynthetic regulation. We extend the Update from ABA-relevant gene discovery to recent advances in multicellular coordination of stomatal control. Growing evidence supports the view that ABA-regulated stomatal movement and gas exchange are coordinated across multiple cell types, including guard cells, mesophyll cells, bundle sheath cells, and vascular tissues in roots and leaves. We also highlight emerging tools to dissect this ABA-mediated multicellular network by using emerging technologies in single-cell and spatial omics, plant optogenetics, and artificial intelligence (AI). These advances will shape ABA research from single cell models toward multicellular collaborative networks for understanding plant-environment interactions. Together, this article links the history of ABA research with emerging single-cell resolution datasets and AI-assisted computational approaches, proposing a framework for moving ABA biology from well-established guard-cell signaling models toward a broader understanding of multicellular ABA coordination.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Perspectives on Source-Sink Dynamics in Plants.
papers.abstract: Source-sink relationships describe how plants coordinate carbon production, transport, and utilization to support growth, reproduction, and stress responses. Classical physiological studies established a robust organ-level framework for carbon allocation, but these approaches largely treat tissues as homogeneous units. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies now reveal that both sources and sinks consist of diverse cell populations with specialized metabolic and transport functions. In this review, we synthesize emerging insights from single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and integrative multi-omics to show how cellular heterogeneity shapes photosynthetic source strength, vascular transport interfaces, and sink development. We further discuss how stress responses, signaling molecules, and plant-associated microbiomes dynamically reprogram source-sink relationships in a spatially structured manner. Finally, we highlight opportunities to integrate high-resolution molecular atlases with physiological modeling and machine learning approaches to develop predictive frameworks for carbon allocation. These advances suggest that future crop improvement strategies will increasingly rely on cell-type-specific engineering of transport processes and metabolic sinks rather than simply enhancing photosynthesis.

papers.title: STADIA: A Spatio-Temporal Deep-Learning Framework for Cross-Stage Integration and Batch Correction of Plant Developmental Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the spatial architecture and transcriptional dynamics of plant organ development to be resolved in situ. However, integrating plant spatial transcriptomic data across developmental stages is challenging because genuine developmental variation can be confounded with technical variation arising from section source, capture region and sequencing batch, making it difficult to attenuate technical effects without compromising developmental signals. To address this challenge, we developed STADIA, a spatio-temporal deep-learning framework for plant developmental spatial transcriptomics. STADIA combines a graph-attention autoencoder with structural-context-conditioned batch-predictability suppression, stage-order constraints, PCGrad-based gradient coordination and hierarchical unbalanced optimal transport to learn an integrated latent representation that attenuates batch-associated variation while preserving spatial organization and developmental continuity and accommodating non-equivalent tissue transitions. In a semi-synthetic benchmark, STADIA maintained balanced performance across batch mixing, anatomical-domain preservation and developmental-information preservation under strong batch effects and high sparsity. In the same-stage replicate sections from the soybean early-maturation stage (EMS), STADIA increased local between-section mixing while retaining major anatomical compartments. In a poplar stem developmental series spanning the shoot apex to internode 7, the integrated representation showed increased cross-stage continuity while retaining stage-specific organization and spatially coherent tissue compartments, and supported exploratory identification of cambium-associated trajectory candidates. Together, these results support STADIA as a framework for cross-stage integration of plant spatial transcriptomic data and for downstream analysis of spatial domains and developmentally ordered transcriptional patterns.

papers.title: Decoding the Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) Niche Microenvironment <i>via</i> Integrative Analysis of Single Cell Multiomics and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, destructive lung disease caused by mutations in TSC1 or TSC2, leading to mTORC1 hyperactivation. While mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, the only FDA approved drug for this disease, stabilizes lung function in most LAM patients, the drug does not eliminate LAM cells, underscoring a critical gap in our understanding of the tumor microenvironment and cellular heterogeneity that drive disease progression. This study provides the first comprehensive multiomics atlas of the human LAM niche, integrating single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq, single-nucleus ATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to deconvolute its complex architecture. We elucidate LAM cellular heterogeneity by identifying three distinct subtypes: the canonical, uterine smooth muscle-like, mTORC1-hyperactive LAM<sup>CORE1</sup>; a novel, fibroblast-like LAM<sup>CORE2</sup> subtype with potent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling activity; and LAM<sup>CORE3</sup>, a substate of LAM<sup>CORE1</sup> that shares LAM and myogenic signatures but is characterized by a lower transcriptional activity and specific functional enrichment in protein translation.Our analysis reveals the transcriptomic heterogeneity of the LAM subtypes, orchestrated by distinct transcriptional drivers and networks. Furthermore, we uncover spatially resolved LAM-associated fibroblast (LAF) states, LAF-seed and LAF-niche, that orchestrate TGF-β signaling, ECM deposition and remodeling, and niche expansion. Spatial mapping uncovers a structured ecosystem where LAM<sup>CORE1</sup> cells form a central core enmeshed with the lymphatic endothelium, which is surrounded by LAFs, LAM<sup>CORE2</sup> cells, and reprogrammed immune and epithelial cells. Findings were validated through multimodal imaging technologies. Present work advances the field by providing the first high-resolution blueprint of the LAM niche microenvironment, revealing novel cell states and crosstalk that identify promising therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal co-transcriptomics uncovers coordinated rhizobia-legume stress programs supporting nitrogen fixation in Medicago.
papers.abstract: Rhizobial nitrogen fixation in legume nodules requires precise spatial and temporal coordination between host and bacterial gene expression. Here, we applied spatial enhanced resolution omics sequencing (Stereo-seq) to profile Medicago nodules across five developmental stages, generating a co-transcriptomic atlas of nodule development. Using a mixed-probe capture strategy, we simultaneously detected host and rhizobial transcripts within the same tissue sections, enabling analysis of host-microbe transcriptional coordination during symbiosis. We identified dynamic changes in host cell composition and developmental trajectories and uncovered two transcription factors, MtERF82 and MtDOF53, required for maintenance of the indeterminate nodule meristem. Rhizobial and host genes exhibited stage- and zone-specific expression patterns along the nodule apex-to-base axis. Notably, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated stress responses in both host cells and rhizobia were linked to symbiotic nitrogen fixation. Functional analyses further showed that MtERF71 and MtCBF1 promote nitrogen fixation by regulating ROS homeostasis and activating key symbiotic genes, highlighting stress signaling as an integral component of mutualistic symbiosis.

papers.title: Single-Nucleus RNA Sequencing Reveals WRKY12a Regulating Secondary Cell Wall Formation During Xylem Differentiation in Rubber Tree.
papers.abstract: Secondary xylem differentiation determines wood structure and function in perennial plants, yet its regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood in Hevea brasiliensis. Here, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from the cambium to mature xylem region in stems, resolving transcriptionally distinct cell populations corresponding to cambium, xylem mother cells, and fibre-vessel cells. Pseudotime analysis reconstructed the developmental trajectories from cambium to late xylem cell states and revealed stage-specific activation of secondary cell wall (SCW) biosynthesis programmes. Gene regulatory network analysis identified HbWRKY12a as a fibre-vessel enriched transcription factor functioning as a key regulator in SCW formation. Molecular assays demonstrated that HbWRKY12a directly binds and activates HbMYB1R1c, which subsequently modulates lignin-associated SCW deposition. Heterologous overexpression of either HbWRKY12a or HbMYB1R1c in Arabidopsis resulted in significant reductions in stem diameter and plant height. Both overexpression lines exhibited markedly decreased SCW thickness in fibre, vessels, and pith cells. These findings reveal a WRKY-MYB cascade that mediates SCW formation in H. brasiliensis, extending the classical NAC-MYB regulatory framework and providing molecular targets for improving xylem properties and stress resilience in tropical perennial crops.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals the Developmental Landscape of Wheat Roots.
papers.abstract: Allohexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is one of the major crops worldwide, however there is very limited research on the transcriptional programmes of underlying cell type specification. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to unravel the transcriptome heterogeneity of cells and the composition of cell types in broad-spectrum organisms. Here, we reported the scRNA-seq transcriptomes of single cells from root tips of the wheat Chinese spring (CS) cultivar, defined cell-type-specific marker genes, and identified most of the major cell types. We further profiled the reconstructed developmental trajectories of the stem cell niche (SCN), proximal meristems and meristems, unveiled gene expression signature of water transportation, divulged cell-type-specific asymmetric gene transcription in subgenomes and explored the evolutionary conservation and divergence of wheat cultivar (CS) and rice cultivar (Nip and 93-11, ZH11) cell types through interspecies comparison. Collectively, this work underscored the transcriptional landscape of wheat cultivar (CS) roots and provided a single-cell perspective for differentiation trajectory application, unbalanced gene expression pattern and characteristics of cell types between two plant species, contributing to a better understanding of wheat cultivar (CS) root development at unprecedented resolution.

papers.title: Mapping the epigenetic regulatory network of cotton single-cell fiber elongation mediated by H3K4me3.
papers.abstract: Histone modifications are central to plant development, yet how they coordinate cellular morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Cotton fibers, as single-celled trichomes derived from seed epidermal cells, provide an ideal model to address this question. Multi-omics approaches were used, including cleavage under targets and tagmentation for genome-wide H3K4me3 profiling and transcriptome sequencing. These were integrated with molecular and genetic validation experiments such as virus-induced gene silencing, overexpression, CRISPR/Cas9, yeast one/two-hybrid, electrophoretic mobility shift assay, co-immunoprecipitation, and split-luciferase complementation assays. We identify GhMYBL as a core transcriptional repressor that negatively regulates fiber elongation. GhMYBL is subject to dual control: H3K4me3 governs its transcription, whereas GhHBI1 posttranslationally attenuates its DNA-binding activity. GhMYBL directly represses the positive regulators GhXTH22 and GhALP1, limiting elongation; GhHBI1 relieves this repression, enabling their normal expression and synergistic promotion of fiber elongation. Our results demonstrate that differential H3K4me3 modification orchestrates GhMYBL-mediated transcriptional repression, which is fine-tuned by GhHBI1 interaction to coordinate fiber cell elongation. This study provides mechanistic insights into the epigenetic control of cell elongation and highlights promising targets for cotton fiber improvement.

papers.title: Integration of single nucleus RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq reveals gene regulatory networks for vascular connection between parasitic plants and host plants.
papers.abstract: The facultative parasitic plant Phtheirospermum japonicum forms a specialized organ, the haustorium, to invade its host, Arabidopsis thaliana, establishing a vascular connection via the formation of a xylem bridge. This connection depends on coordinated interactions between the vascular systems of both plants, yet the molecular dynamics of these interactions within the haustorium and the host roots remain elusive. This study aimed to unravel the transcriptomic heterogeneity of haustoria and gene regulatory networks involved in this process by integrating single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq). snRNA-seq identified a total of 7 P. japonicum cell clusters and 4 A. thaliana cell clusters, each with cluster-specific marker genes, allowing for a distinct characterization of vascular cells within the haustorium. Differential gene expression analyses revealed up-regulation of genes associated with xylem formation and auxin transport in both parasites and hosts, suggesting the presence of shared molecular mechanisms facilitating vascular connection. Further gene network analysis combining snRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq identified conserved homologous genes across both species, indicating potential molecular interactions of vascular-related genes from hosts and parasites. Our study reveals the high heterogeneity of haustorium cells, characterizing the expression profiles of each cell type in haustoria and host roots during haustorium development at single-cell resolution. These findings provide insights into the molecular interactions between parasitic plants and hosts, presenting potential targets for disrupting these interactions to manage parasitic plant infestations in crops.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics unveils photosynthetic adaptation in submersed leaves of heterophyllous Nuphar pumila.
papers.abstract: C4 photosynthesis has emerged in various plant lineages as an adaptive response to abiotic stress, as it allows for higher photosynthetic efficiency. C4 photosynthesis has been uncovered in both terrestrial and aquatic plants. However, the extent to which C4 photosynthesis serves as an adaptation to submerged environments in aquatic plants remains elusive. Here, we studied the heterophyllous aquatic plant Nuphar pumila, which has phenotypically distinct leaves depending on the level of submergence. By applying 13C labeling experiments, submersed leaves of N. pumila were shown to exhibit both C4 and C3 photosynthesis, whereas floating leaves are limited to C3 photosynthesis. Leaf-specific single-cell trajectories of epidermal and bundle sheath cells show that, in contrast to terrestrial C4 plants, CO2 fixation in C4 photosynthesis in submersed leaves primarily occurs in the epidermal cells rather than in the mesophyll cells, allowing the leaves to cope with limited inorganic carbon in water. The combined presence of C3 and C4 photosynthesis, along with tissue-specific adaptations in the heterophyllous aquatic plant N. pumila, demonstrates how C4 photosynthesis in aquatic environments likely evolved as an adaptive trait from C3 photosynthesis.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptional profiling in Arabidopsis root exposed to boron toxicity at seedling stages.
papers.abstract: Cell-specific transcriptional responses to environmental stimuli are yet to be fully characterized. Single-cell sequencing technology allows us to analyze different cell types under different conditions. Here, high-throughput single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed in Arabidopsis thaliana roots exposed to different B toxicity conditions by using a commercially available droplet-based microfluidics platform (10xGenomics) to understand how B toxicity altered gene expression and development at single-cell resolution. Accordingly, we found that 2755 cells could be annotated using cell-specific marker genes into 10 cell-type clusters including lateral root cap + epidermis + quiescent cells (QC) + columella, stele, cortex, cortex + endodermis, metaxylem, columella, trichoblast, pericycle initial cells + protoxylem, metapholem and phloem. Upregulated genes were highly associated with glutathione and sulfur metabolism in the columella, endodermis, and QC under B toxicity. Further analysis revealed that upregulated genes were highly correlated with the ribosome pathway in lateral root cap + epidermis + quiescent cells + columella, stele, and cortex clusters. Moreover, we identified the transcription factors at the cortex, lateral root cap + epidermis + quiescent cells + columella, cortex + endodermis, and trichoblast cell clusters in Arabidopsis root under severe B toxicity conditions. Taken together, for the first time in the literature, our study provides a gene expression map at single-cell resolution and describes the extent of heterogeneity at the molecular level among populations of different cell types in Arabidopsis root under B toxicity conditions and will significantly promote the investigation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the B toxicity.

papers.title: Research on Bamboo Shoot Bud Development: A Leap from Tissue Heterogeneity to Single-Cell Spatial Atlas.
papers.abstract: China has rich bamboo resources, with Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) being the most economically important species. Bamboo shoot bud development directly determines the eating quality of the shoots and the properties of bamboo materials; however, the intrinsic biological characteristics of this process have hindered foundational research. Traditional methods using whole shoot buds or mixed tissues obscure cellular and tissue heterogeneity, limiting our mechanistic understanding. This review synthesizes cytological features, molecular networks, and technical limitations pertaining to Moso bamboo shoot bud development, identifying four key bottlenecks: tissue homogenization masking cellular heterogeneity, loss of spatial positional information impeding analysis of position effects, challenges in single-cell technology application due to sample preparation and data interpretation issues, and unresolved coupling between chromatin accessibility and transcriptional regulation. To address these, we propose a core strategy centered on constructing a single-cell resolution, spatially resolved, multi-omics integrated, and functionally validated framework. Key approaches include developing bamboo-specific single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, integrating positional information with multi-omics data to identify spatially distinct regulatory targets, standardizing technical pipelines and functional validation platforms, and elucidating epigenetic-transcriptional coupling. Overcoming these bottlenecks will reveal the molecular basis of bamboo's unique developmental patterns and provide key targets for the genetic improvement of the shoot quality and mechanical properties of bamboo.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptional regulatory networks governing cereal root responses to heavy metals and drought.
papers.abstract: Cereal root systems perceive the onset of drought and heavy metal toxicity, which rapidly triggers signal transduction and extensive transcriptional reprogramming that underpins plant stress tolerance. This review discusses the transcriptional basis of root responses to abiotic stresses, emphasizing key regulatory genes and networks that orchestrate hormone signaling, redox dynamics, ion homeostasis, and structural modifications. Key transcription factor families-NAC, WRKY, bZIP, DREB, ARF, and MYB-serve as the nexus between the early perception and adaptive outputs such as controlled root growth, suberization, aerenchyma formation, and metal sequestration. Integrative transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and chromatin data in rice, wheat, maize, and millets highlight cell-type- and zone-specific regulatory programs, with single-cell and spatial omics uncovering modules obscured in bulk datasets. We discuss how CRISPR/Cas editing, cis-element engineering, and root-specific promoters refine core regulators, and how quantitative trait loci (QTL)/genome-wide association study (GWAS) advance breeding for drought and metal tolerance. Emerging concepts encompass multi-stress omics, high-throughput root phenomics, and artificial intelligence-driven network modeling, and collectively enable targeting of core transcriptional regulatory nodes. Overall, emerging knowledge supports targeted engineering of transcriptional regulators to develop resilient cereal root systems, contributing to sustainable yields and improved stress tolerance in real-world agroecosystems.

papers.title: Paired bulk transcriptomic analysis of recurrent glioblastoma with primary single-cell reference mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, and virtually all patients relapse on standard temozolomide (TMZ) plus radiotherapy. The molecular mechanisms that allow residual tumor cells to survive treatment, reshape the microenvironment, and seed a drug-resistant recurrence remain incompletely understood. We analyzed paired bulk RNA-seq from 13 primary-recurrent patient pairs (GSE139533), used two published primary GBM single-cell/single-nucleus samples (GSE138794/GSM4119534 and GSE174554/GSM5319503; 5244 quality-controlled cells/nuclei) solely for cellular-context mapping, and evaluated an exploratory bulk-derived gene set in TCGA-GBM. Paired testing of 18,445 genes identified one significant gene at FDR 〈 0.05 and |log2FC| 〉 0.3: IL4I1 (log2FC = 1.49, FDR = 0.023). A 40-gene exploratory set was defined as the 40 positive paired-effect genes with the strongest paired-test evidence in the same 13 pairs and used descriptively; its mean paired score difference was 1.02 z-score units, but no independent significance test was assigned to this within-cohort score. In the primary single-cell references, the set scored highest in Myeloid-like cells, providing cellular context without constituting a primary-recurrent single-cell comparison. TCGA-GBM showed a weak, non-significant baseline survival association (Cox HR 1.30, 95% CI 0.91-1.87, P = 0.15). A TMZ-resistant U251 derivative had a higher TMZ IC50 than parental cells (612 vs 89 µM), and Western blotting showed increased MGMT, CD44, Vimentin, HIF-1α, OPN and PD-L1 across three biological experiments. Together, these data provide a paired bulk description of recurrence-associated expression and use primary single-cell references only to localize the exploratory signal.

papers.title: Plant embryogenesis from zygotic genome activation to seed maturation: Comparative mechanisms and engineering opportunities.
papers.abstract: Plant embryogenesis converts a zygote into a patterned, maturation-competent embryo. Since the major syntheses published in 2019 and 2021, allele-resolved transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial profiling, and three-dimensional imaging have revealed substantial variation in zygotic genome activation and cleavage geometry across angiosperms, challenging models derived solely from Arabidopsis. Here, we organize recent advances along a comparative zygote-to-seed trajectory and ask how conserved regulatory modules are redeployed across lineages, how early patterning is coupled to seed maturation, and which developmental transitions can be engineered in crops. We first compare the maternal-to-zygotic transition and associated chromatin-state changes, explicitly distinguishing observations from hypotheses about their evolutionary drivers. We then examine how PIN-FORMED (PIN)-dependent auxin transport, local auxin biosynthesis, membrane and peptide signaling, and WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX (WOX)-family transcription factors establish embryonic axes and meristems. Next, we connect these early programs to source-sink relations, nutrient partitioning, proteostasis, and hormone-redox control during seed maturation, while separating maturation from dormancy release and germination. Finally, we assess how spatial multi-omics, live imaging, CRISPR activation, and synthetic apomixis can interrogate or engineer these transitions. This framework identifies conserved modules, lineage-specific solutions, and major evidence gaps that must be resolved before embryogenesis can be predictably manipulated for crop improvement.

papers.title: Advances in gene editing for legume improvement: technologies, progress, and prospects.
papers.abstract: Legumes are among the most important protein-rich crops in global agri-food systems. To meet the rising protein demand of a growing population, significant efforts are underway to enhance legume yield, nutritional quality, and resilience to environmental stresses through the manipulation of key genetic traits. Advanced technologies-including genetic engineering, gene editing, genomic selection, next-generation sequencing, single-cell genomics, and multi-omics-are accelerating legume improvement due to their high precision and efficiency. This review focuses on major gene-editing technologies, namely, CRISPR/Cas9 (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR-associated protein 9), TALENs (Transcription Activator-Like Effector Nucleases), ZFNs (Zinc Finger Nucleases), base editing (BE), and prime editing (PE), and their applications in key legume crops such as soybean (Glycine max), cowpea (Vigna unguiculata), chickpea (Cicer arietinum), groundnut (Arachis hypogaea), pea (Pisum sativum), barrel clover (Medicago truncatula), alfalfa (Medicago sativa), and Lotus japonicus. Among these platforms, CRISPR/Cas9 is the most widely adopted in legumes, largely due to its simplicity, versatility, and dependence on accurate genome sequence information and guide RNA (gRNA) design. Advances in next-generation sequencing and the growing availability of intuitive online gRNA design tools have streamlined CRISPR workflows, improving accessibility and precision. The present review indicates that CRISPR-P is the most used gRNA design tool in legume research, likely due to its early development for plant systems and integrated off-target prediction features. Therefore, alongside reviewing gene-editing applications, we emphasized the critical role of robust gRNA design tools as a foundation for successful genome editing. Future integration of artificial intelligence and large language models is expected to further enhance target prediction accuracy, minimize off-target effects, and enable more precise genome-editing strategies in legumes.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals a conserved GA-GASA1-ROS module that promotes lateral root founder cell specification.
papers.abstract: The specification and commitment of lateral root founder cells (LRFCs) from postembryonic pericycle cells are critical steps in LR development, but their earliest molecular determinants remain unclear. Using single-cell transcriptomics, we resolved the transcriptional transitions that guide LRFC fate in Arabidopsis thaliana and identified five distinct phases of transcriptional progression during LRFC specification. Through analysis of differentially expressed genes and phenotypic observations, we showed that application of exogenous gibberellin (GA; 20 and 50 μM) promoted nuclear migration and division in LRFCs independently of DELLA signaling and revealed that gibberellic-acid-stimulated Arabidopsis 1 (GASA1) functions as a key mediator of GA to accelerate LRFC progression. Histochemical staining and cytological observations demonstrated that GASA1 mediates GA-triggered accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) to reinforce LRFC commitment. The GA-GASA1-ROS module is evolutionarily conserved, and GA-ROS-driven LRFC commitment is fundamental across angiosperms. Notably, GASA1 emerged during root evolution in early land plants and diversified alongside lateral and shoot-borne root systems, revealing a conserved GA-ROS axis in plant organogenesis.

papers.title: Spatial isoform sequencing at single-cell resolution reveals cell-type-specific spatial isoform variability in multiple brain cell types.
papers.abstract: Spatial long-read technologies are increasingly common but usually lack single-cell resolution. This leaves unanswered whether spatially variable isoforms reflect variability within one cell type or differences in region-specific cell-type composition. Here, we developed Spl-ISO-Seq2 (500-nm resolution) and accompanying software, Spl-IsoQuant-2 and Spl-IsoFind, enabling long-read sequencing of >450 million barcodes versus 80,000 previously. Applying this to the adult mouse brain, we compared differential isoform abundance between known regions and spatial isoform patterns independent of predefined regions. Both identified overlapping hits, for example, Rps24 in oligodendrocytes. For known Snap25 spatial isoform variation, we show that it occurs in excitatory neurons. The region-agnostic approach also uncovered patterns missed by region-based comparisons, for example, for Ighm. Notably, many spatial isoform signals are not driven by cell-type composition alone. Finally, our software is applicable to many spatial and single-cell protocols, demonstrating reproducibility between platforms (for example, Visium HD/Stereo-seq). Overall, our experimental/analytical methods enable a submicron-resolution-isoform view and open avenues for spatial isoform disease research.

papers.title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root.
papers.abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

papers.title: Beyond phosphate uptake: PT4/PT11 as key functional components linking phosphate acquisition, nutrient exchange, and arbuscule maintenance in arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis.
papers.abstract: Phosphorus is an essential macronutrient for plant growth and development, yet its availability in many soils is limited by strong chemical fixation and low mobility. Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis provides an important biological strategy for improving plant phosphate acquisition by establishing specialized arbuscules within root cortical cells, where reciprocal nutrient exchange occurs across the periarbuscular membrane (PAM). Among the phosphate transporter families involved in this process, the mycorrhiza-specific PHT1 transporters PT4 in Medicago truncatula and PT11 in Oryza sativa are major components of the mycorrhizal phosphate uptake pathway and are required for efficient phosphate acquisition and the maintenance of functional arbuscules. Genetic and physiological studies further indicate that disruption of PT4/PT11-mediated phosphate transport is closely associated with premature arbuscule degeneration and impaired symbiotic performance, highlighting a functional link between phosphate uptake, nutrient exchange, and arbuscule maintenance. In this review, we summarize current knowledge of the molecular mechanisms underlying PT4/PT11 function and regulation during AM symbiosis. We first compare mycorrhiza-specific phosphate transporters across plant species and discuss their localization, transport properties, and contributions to the mycorrhizal Pi uptake pathway. We then examine the multilayered regulatory network controlling PT4/PT11 expression, including the common symbiosis signaling pathway, calcium-dependent signaling, CYCLOPS-RAM1-centered transcriptional regulation, AP2/ERF-family regulators, hormone-associated regulation, and systemic phosphate-sensing pathways. Particular attention is given to the functional coupling between PT4/PT11-mediated phosphate uptake and other components of reciprocal nutrient exchange, including carbon and lipid transfer, proton extrusion, and arbuscule maintenance. We further discuss how impairment of phosphate transport through PT4/PT11 affects arbuscule integrity and the physiological conditions of the plant-fungus interface. Based on available genetic and physiological evidence, we propose a working model in which PT4/PT11-mediated phosphate uptake contributes to maintaining a favorable interfacial phosphate environment and efficient nutrient exchange, thereby supporting arbuscule function and longevity. Importantly, current evidence does not demonstrate that PT4/PT11 possess a transport-independent function or directly transmit signals through interactions with downstream signaling components. The mechanisms linking transporter activity, local phosphate status, nutrient exchange, and arbuscule maintenance therefore remain to be experimentally resolved. Finally, we highlight emerging approaches, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, proximity labeling, transport-defective mutants, and genome editing, that may distinguish transport-dependent from potential transport-independent functions of PT4/PT11. Understanding these mechanisms may provide a conceptual and practical foundation for exploiting AM symbiosis to improve phosphorus-use efficiency, reduce dependence on mineral phosphate fertilizers, and develop more sustainable crop production systems.

papers.title: Single-cell laser ablation uncovers the blueprint of plant development.
papers.abstract: Understanding how positional information within plant tissues shapes developmental programs in real time has long remained a challenge due to technical limitations in precisely accessing and manipulating defined cellular domains within complex tissues. Recent advances in single-cell laser ablation, particularly when combined with confocal microscopy, now allow precise spatiotemporal perturbation of selected cells. This technology has enabled researchers to dissect cellular functions, communication dynamics, and mechanical responses with unprecedented accuracy. Here, we review how laser ablation has emerged as a transformative approach in plant biology, from unraveling the signaling networks governing meristem maintenance and root patterning to modeling wound responses and immune activation.

papers.title: Single-Cell Mapping of the Gut Epithelium Reveals Paneth Cell Dysfunction and Lysozyme Deficiency in Peanut Allergy.
papers.abstract:
Background & aims

A growing body of evidence links intestinal epithelial cell barrier dysfunction to the development of food allergies. We previously showed that the peanut allergy-susceptible CC027 mouse has increased intestinal permeability. To understand the heterogeneity of the intestinal barrier in peanut allergy susceptibility, we used single-cell RNA sequencing to generate a high-resolution single-cell atlas of the small intestinal epithelium in the naïve CC027 mouse. This can be used to inform patient findings and provide a resource for understanding how epithelial cells contribute to peanut allergy pathogenesis.

Methods

We generated a high-resolution single-cell atlas of the intestinal epithelium of allergy-susceptible, naïve CC027 mice and allergy-prone but orally resistant, naïve C3H/HeJ mice. Histology studies in gastrointestinal tissues from mice and human patients with or without peanut allergy corroborated our findings.

Results

Naïve CC027 mice exhibited a reduced proportion of interferon-responsive absorptive enterocytes compared with naïve C3H/HeJ mice, reduced numbers of enteroendocrine cells, and increased numbers of goblet and tuft cells. We found a complete absence of the Paneth cell antimicrobial peptide lysozyme 1 transcript and enrichment of mitochondrial stress pathways in peanut unexposed CC027 mice. Paneth cells from CC027 mice exhibited signs of cell stress by electron microscopy. In patients with peanut allergy, small intestinal biopsies demonstrated decreased Paneth cell-specific lysozyme 1 protein expression.

Conclusions

We establish a single-cell atlas of the intestinal epithelium in a translationally relevant peanut allergy-susceptible mouse model and show a link between intestinal permeability, epithelial-derived interferon responses, and Paneth cell dysfunction in maintaining immune tolerance to dietary antigens.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals metabolic reprogramming and CTH downregulation in diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract:
Objective

To characterize metabolic and transcriptional alterations in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and identify diagnostic biomarkers using a multi-omics approach.

Materials and methods

Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess causal relationships between metabolites and DKD. Renal transcriptomic datasets validated pathway and gene alterations. Machine learning models evaluated diagnostic performance, with SHAP for interpretation. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics defined cell-specific expression patterns. In silico gene perturbation and in vitro validation in high-glucose-treated HK-2 cells were conducted.

Results

MR analysis identified 60 plasma metabolites whose genetically predicted levels showed evidence of association with DKD. These metabolites were enriched in one-carbon metabolism, histidine metabolism, and glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, which showed consistent alterations in renal transcriptomic analyses. Machine learning models showed strong diagnostic performance (mean AUC = 0.963), with MAOA, CTH, and ALDH1L1 as key contributors. CTH was specifically expressed in proximal tubular cells and downregulated in injury-associated subpopulations. Functional analyses indicated that CTH affected epithelial integrity, mitochondrial metabolism, and immune responses, and was suppressed under high-glucose conditions.

Conclusion

These findings provide insight into DKD pathogenesis and highlight CTH as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Multi-Generational High Nitrogen Application Inhibits Seed Germination in Wheat: Insights Into Metabolic Dynamics and Microbial Interactions.
papers.abstract: Excessive nitrogen (N) application can affect soil health and crop performance, yet the multi-generational effects of prolonged high-N exposure on wheat seed germination remain unclear. We profiled seed metabolomes and endophytic bacterial communities across seven consecutive wheat generations (F1-F7) under normal-N and high-N regimes, and assessed germination of F7 seeds. Spatial metabolomics, spatial transcriptomics and 16S rRNA sequencing were used to resolve embryo- and endosperm-specific responses. Seven generations of high-N treatment delayed progeny seed germination and decreased the germination index by 12.3%, whereas the vigor index was not significantly affected. Spatial omics revealed strong embryo-endosperm heterogeneity and a high-N-associated shift in endosperm metabolism, including a 73.9% decrease in endosperm L-aspartic acid. Compartment-resolved microbiome analysis showed enrichment of Bacillus under high-N exposure. Functional assays showed that L-aspartic acid promoted germination/early outgrowth, whereas Bacillus grew with L-aspartic acid as the sole C/N source and reduced germination under L-aspartic acid-supplemented conditions. These results support a model in which multi-generational high N reduces wheat seed germination through endosperm amino-acid depletion and altered endophytic bacterial assembly.

papers.title: Automating the bottleneck: a scalable deep learning pipeline for phytolith detection, imaging, and curation across single-cell and multi-cell morphotypes.
papers.abstract: Deep learning offers powerful tools for automating phytolith classification. Although foundational models have enabled image classification with little or no task specific training, specialized domains such as phytolith images still require a labor-intensive process to acquire labelled training data. This article presents a novel, scalable imaging workflow that addresses this bottleneck by integrating low-magnification slide scanning with artificial intelligence assisted phytolith detection and targeted high-magnification 3D Z-stack capture optimized for both multi-cell and single-cell phytoliths. Automated pre-processing enables imaging of 16 slides per week generating 100's of curated phytolith training images per slide. Developed in collaboration with Nikon Imaging Specialists and validated on 34 comparative grass and rush taxa, the system combines expert-guided sampling with customized automated acquisition routines to capture, segment, tile and curate images for deep learning input. Key workflow optimizations, including hardware upgrades, asynchronous file conversion, and iterative refinement of the artificial intelligence detection model, achieved a 350% improvement in extended depth of field rendering speed and a 55,450% improvement in TIFF export speed, enabling sustained high-throughput acquisition without performance degradation. The workflow was designed to optimize imaging of mixed multi-cell and single-cell phytolith assemblages and is currently generating training data for DL models targeting wild versus domesticated wheat discrimination in addition to grass species identification from multi-cell husk phytolith morphology. Beyond phytoliths, the pipeline is modular, replicable across microscopy platforms, and readily adaptable to other plant microfossils and microstructures, including pollen, starch grains and other silica bodies, through targeted artificial intelligence retraining, making large-scale machine learning applications in plant science, paleoethnobotany and related fields more accessible and reproducible.

papers.title: Combining a high-caliber chromosome-level genome and root single-cell atlas resolves genetic diversity and root development in Olea europaea subsp. cuspidata.
papers.abstract: Olea europaea subsp. cuspidata, a subspecies of olive trees, stands out for its remarkable stress tolerance, and commonly serves as a rootstock that enhances olive oil yield. To explore its genomic and cellular underpinnings for potential breeding applications, a chromosome-scale genome assembly and a root-specific single-cell atlas of O. europaea subsp. cuspidata was resolved. Using a combined survey evaluation strategy along with PacBio CLR and Hi-C sequencing technologies, a total genome of 1.62 Gb was obtained (23 chromosomes; N50: 55.72 Mb). Phylogenetic analysis revealed that Oleaceae plants diverged ∼17.2 million years ago (Mya), with O. europaea subsp. cuspidata splitting from other O. europaea lineages ∼5.7 Mya. It is genetically closer to the cultivated olive O. europaea subsp. europaea cv. Arbequina than to the wild olive O. europaea subsp. europaea var. sylvestris. Additionally, a dynamic molecular map of olive roots was generated at single-cell resolution to reconstruct the continuous root cell differentiation and developmental trajectory. This helps to unravel key regulatory genes in olive root development and adaptation to the external environment. This study explored the diversity of olive trees at genomic and root cellular levels, with insights to support the theoretical basis for enhanced stress tolerance, aiding the global introduction and promotion of olive trees.

papers.title: Identification of Phloem Cell Transcriptome via Single-Cell RNA-Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting cellular heterogeneity in plants at a high resolution. In particular, scRNA-seq has been applied to unravel the complex cell identities and regulatory networks of distinct phloem cell types. Because phloem cells are small and under high osmotic pressure, isolating and maintaining viable protoplasts is a challenge for successful phloem scRNA-seq. Here, we present an optimized protocol for isolating vasculature-enriched protoplasts from mature Arabidopsis thaliana leaves. Following tissue harvesting, protoplasting is performed using a cocktail of cell wall-degrading enzymes suspended in an osmotically stabilized buffer. The resulting cell suspension is purified by removing debris through subsequent wash steps and validated using phloem-specific markers. Besides providing a reliable and reproducible method for isolating high-purity phloem-enriched protoplasts, we introduce the basic pipeline for downstream analysis.

papers.title: Unravelling the multifunctional roles of plant LIM proteins in growth, development, and stress responses.
papers.abstract: LIM (Lin-11, Isl-1, and Mec-3 domain) proteins are evolutionarily conserved proteins that regulate diverse cellular processes in plants, including actin cytoskeleton organization, organ size determination, protein stability, and transcription-associated regulation. Therefore, these proteins have emerged as important regulators of plant growth, development, and responses to biotic and abiotic stresses. Numerous genome-wide studies, functional analyses, and mechanistic investigations in diverse plant species have considerably expanded our understanding of this gene family. However, these advances remain dispersed across the literature, present in peace-meal and have not been critically synthesized. This review summarizes recent progress in the classification and evolutionary diversification of plant LIM proteins, genome-wide identification and comparative analyses, and their multifunctional roles in plant growth and development, including organ size regulation, pollen and fibre development, and vascular differentiation. The review further critically evaluates current evidence for the involvement of LIM proteins in plant immunity and abiotic stress responses by distinguishing expression-based, functional, and mechanistic studies. Finally, the review discusses major knowledge gaps and highlights emerging research directions, including single-cell and spatial omics, phosphoproteomics, interactomics, and CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing, to advance mechanistic understanding and facilitate the exploitation of LIM proteins for crop improvement.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in spatial transcriptomics: a review of methods, datasets, and directions.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) measures gene expression while retaining the location of transcripts or cells within tissue sections. Unlike bulk RNA sequencing, which averages expression across cell populations, and single-cell RNA sequencing, which generally requires tissue dissociation, ST links molecular profiles to tissue architecture. This spatial information supports the analysis of tissue heterogeneity, cellular organization, and potential intercellular interactions. The spatially resolved nature of ST has unlocked diverse applications in fields such as cancer, neuroscience, reproductive biology, and plant biology. In parallel, the development of publicly accessible databases and repositories has facilitated large-scale, multi-cohort comparisons and benchmarking. The rapid expansion and increasing complexity of these datasets have driven the adoption of machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. These computational tools support a range of tasks, including data pre-processing, image segmentation, spatial domain identification, and pattern recognition. Moreover, they are instrumental in integrative multi-omics analyses and predictive modeling. This AI-focused review provides necessary background on ST technologies and databases and evaluates the use of statistical, ML, and DL methods across the analytical workflow, from image and sequencing-data preprocessing to spatial analysis and LLM-assisted interpretation. We compile key resources related to datasets, AI-driven analytical frameworks, and ST data analysis pipelines, and discuss current challenges, limitations, and future directions for AI-based tools in spatial omics.

papers.title: Developmental and Regulatory Framework of Shoot Branching in Plants.
papers.abstract: How do plants build a branch? Shoot branching is a fundamental determinant of plant architecture and is best understood as a dynamic developmental program governed by the coordinated action of multiple regulatory processes rather than by isolated pathways. Branch formation proceeds through a series of coordinated developmental transitions, from axillary meristem initiation and bud establishment to dormancy, activation, and sustained branch outgrowth, driven by interactions among phytohormones, transcription factors, environmental cues, and cellular processes. Here, we propose a developmental framework that integrates these successive stages and synthesize recent advances from both herbaceous and woody plants to illustrate how hormonal, transcriptional, and environmental signals coordinate branch development. We further highlight that these regulatory networks ultimately converge on fundamental cellular processes-including cell cycle progression, vascular differentiation, cell wall remodeling, and mechanical regulation-to execute branch formation. Finally, we discuss the evolutionary diversification of branching mechanisms and emerging technologies, including single-cell and spatial omics, comparative genomics, and artificial intelligence, that are advancing our understanding of shoot branching and accelerating the molecular design of plant architecture.
